thread:
incidents-bot: PAGER: High batching queue depth detected for /v1/generate (hosted). Errors rising, p95 latency spiking, multiple customers reporting 5xx. Auto-escalation to oncall.

alex: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Paging into thread. Can someone grab quick impact numbers?

support-bot: Quick summary: ~2.4% 5xx across gen endpoints in last 5m, top affected clients: shoplytics (1.2% of total errors), convoAI (0.6%), internal-loadtest (0.3%). About 8k reqs/min at peak.

sam: I see GPU queue depth on pool-g-1 at 85%, continuous batching backlog growing. Looks like a surge of many small requests generating lots of tiny batches.

lee: Confirmed. Batching window currently set to 50ms, min-batch-size 2, max-batch-size 64. Lots of small single-request batches causing overhead.

alex: Two levers here: (A) increase batching.window_ms to accumulate larger batches -> better throughput but higher per-request latency, or (B) tighten per-key rate limits / throttle noisy customers -> reduces traffic quickly. I want a hybrid: immediate soft throttles + raise batching window moderately.

maria: Agreed. For immediate mitigation: apply temporary per-key QPS caps for free and trial tiers, and disable reranker/long-context on high-traffic keys. Then bump batching.window_ms to 250ms (from 50ms) to reduce scheduler pressure.

carol: +1. We should avoid full feature kill unless needed. Reranker is expensive per-request. If we can disable rerank for free/trial tiers that's low customer impact.

alex: Doing opsctl commands now. Will post outputs.

alex: ```
# throttle free tier QPS
opsctl quota set --tier free --qps 4 --reason "emergency batching overload 1898765432"
# disable reranker for free & trial
opsctl feature-toggle set reranker --tier free --state off --reason "emergency"
# increase continuous batching window to 250ms
opsctl route update /v1/generate --batching.window_ms=250 --batching.max_batch_size=128
```

ops-bot: opsctl: started job 0x7f3c. Applying quota changes and route config.

ops-bot: opsctl: job 0x7f3c completed successfully. Changes rolled to 3 clusters (hosted-us, hosted-eu, hosted-ap).

sam: Seeing immediate drop in scheduler churn. GPU queue depth down to 60% in pool-g-1 within 90s.

support-bot: Customer impact update: 5xx rate down to ~0.4% in last 3m. Minor increase in p50/p95 latency for gen: p50 from 60ms -> 180ms, p95 from 500ms -> ~1.1s. Top customers see fewer errors, but shoplytics reported higher end-to-end latency on long prompt flows.

lee: Tradeoff expected: we intentionally increased batching to improve throughput and reduce tail queueing. We should watch interactive UX customers.

maria: For interactive customers we can add routing policy to send their traffic to low-latency pool with tighter latency SLO (if capacity allows). For now, we need the outage stabilized.

carol: Can we tighten burst window instead of global bump? Maybe do per-route: /v1/generate-interactive keep at 50ms, apply 250ms only for bulk-generate route.

alex: Good call. I'll rollback the global change and make it per-route to avoid impacting interactive endpoints. Executing:```
opsctl route update /v1/generate-interactive --batching.window_ms=50
opsctl route update /v1/generate-bulk --batching.window_ms=250 --batching.max_batch_size=256
```

ops-bot: opsctl: started job 0x7f4d. Applying per-route batching windows.

ops-bot: opsctl: job 0x7f4d completed.

sam: Metrics: /v1/generate-interactive p50 ~70ms, p95 ~330ms. /v1/generate-bulk p50 ~210ms, p95 ~1.3s. Overall 5xx ~0.2%. GPU utilization more stable.

alex: Noting actions: temporary free-tier QPS cap, reranker off for free/trial, per-route batching windows (interactive=50ms, bulk=250ms).

support-bot: Logged customer tickets impacted: #PROD-4321 (shoplytics), #PROD-4322 (convoAI). Support messages updated, CS notified.

maria: I'll take the rest of the oncall window. alex, can you do handoff summary?

alex: Handoff: I applied emergency throttles and adjusted batching config per-route. Error rate reduced from ~2.4% -> 0.2%. Latency increased for bulk customers (expected). Key follow-ups: 1) Evaluate why surge had so many tiny requests (client-side retry storm or SDK bug), 2) Add smarter adaptive batching that grows window under high backlog but isolates interactive paths, 3) Postmortem and customer comms draft.

alex: I'm logging off in 35m; maria will be primary now. If things degrade revert batching.window_ms back down and re-enable reranker if safe.

maria: Got it. I'll monitor for 2h and start a post-incident runbook entry. Also scheduling a canary to gradually ramp free-tier QPS back starting +30m if 5xx stays low.

lee: For the long-term: we should add continuous-batching autotuner that considers request shape distribution and critical route tags. Also add alert for disproportionate small-batch fraction.

carol: I'll open an RFC for feature-gating expensive features by route and tier.

support-bot: Final snapshot before handoff: p95 overall ~1.1s, p50 ~200ms, 5xx ~0.18%. Ops changes in place and documented.

maria: Thanks all. I'll run the postmortem template and loop in product and support for customer comms. Leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
